{"id":"mimid-1wgh.116","title":"Decision: a call announcement is a private-use text extension key, "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call"","description":"Mark decided 2026-11-23, for bead mimid-1wgh.114.1.

THE QUESTION. A call is a parent-dependent room with its own MLS group
and its own exported media secret (bead mimid-1wgh.108). Nothing in MIMI
says a call is LIVE (bead mimid-1wgh.37.111). So how does a message in
the parent chat announce one?

THE TEXT. mimi-content-10 §4.3: "Each extension has a CBOR map key which
is a positive integer, negative integer, or text string containing
between 1 and 255 octets of UTF-8. The value can be any CBOR (including
combinations of maps and arrays)." And: "An IANA registry Section 8.2.1
is defined for positive integer keys. Negative integer and text string
keys are only for private use."

§8.2.1 adds, of the registry's Type column: "Applications with multiple,
related data items are encouraged to register a map type that contains
all the related fields."

REJECTED FIRST, and it is why this bead exists: carrying the call room's
URI in a §5.10 session part. §5.10 is about EXTERNAL conference URLs in
its own prose, and a mimi:// room URI has no defined join behaviour
anywhere, so the field would have carried a private extension that looked
standard. Bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 has the reasoning.

COMPETING SPELLINGS, both private use under §4.3:
(a) A negative integer, e.g. -1.
(b) A text string, domain-qualified: "reviewcommit.com/call", the
    convention IRC uses (soju.im/webpush).
(c) A text string naming the defining document:
    "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call".

CHOSEN: (c), the text string "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call", with a map
value. INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC.

WHY:
- (a) collides. Two implementations each reaching for a private negative
  integer both pick something small and obvious. Two picking text strings
  do not, because a string carries its own namespace. There is no
  coordination between us and Haven on this.
- (a) also tells a reader of the wire nothing. A key is visible; it
  should name itself.
- (c) over (b): a domain says WHO defined it, the draft name says WHERE
  IT IS WRITTEN DOWN, and for a provisional key the second is what a
  reader needs. The draft carries Mark's name either way.
- 28 octets, against §4.3's limit of 255, and an announcement is one
  message per call, so the size does not matter.
- It is meant to be thrown away. When §8.2.1 assigns a positive integer
  the string goes, and naming the draft makes that transition legible:
  the string and the registry entry point at the same document. Same
  shape as the provisional ComponentID of decision mimid-1wgh.112.

THE VALUE: a CBOR map with text keys, one entry to begin with:

  "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call": { "room": "mimi://a.example/r/<call>" }

A map rather than a bare URI string because §8.2.1 encourages one for
related fields, and because whatever a call announcement turns out to
need next -- who started it, when, whether it ended -- goes in without
burning a second key.

IMPLEMENTATION COST is near zero: mimi_content::extension::ExtensionKey
already has a Text(String) variant with §4.3's 1-to-255-octet bound, and
its own comment says "for private use", so the codec round-trips this
today. A map at that position is nesting level 2, inside
MAX_EXTENSION_DEPTH of 4.

NOT DECIDED HERE, and it is the next question: how a client learns the
call ENDED. Without an answer a client shows "call in progress" forever.
The room cannot answer it for someone who never joined the call -- they
are in the parent chat, not the call room, so they cannot see its
membership. That points at a second announcement, which can be lost if
the announcer crashes, which means a client must treat it as advisory.
Its own decision.
